svg.title: AsyncPP ideal load-back
svg.desc: Fully asynchronous PP, ideal load-back timing (schematic)
svg.text: Fully asynchronous PP, ideal load-back timing (schematic)
If PP0's decision for micro-batch j reached every stage at once, every stage could start loading j's prefix KV right then, long before its forward.
The load-back then never sits on a forward's critical path. Cost: KV pages are taken earlier.
What it takes, and what it costs
0. Gain: forward j no longer waits for its load-back. Measured, that wait is 0.67-0.85 ms per forward on the bottleneck stages (at most 0.5% of the beat).
1. PP0's decision must reach every stage directly, not hop by hop: one epoch record fanned out by PP0 (P2, "epoch control channel").
2. The copy may no longer wait for the whole forward stream (today: host_to_device_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)); it may only wait
for the pages it overwrites, i.e. for this stage's queued forwards that still read pages freed in the last few epochs.
3. Cost: a stage takes j's KV pages when PP0 decides j instead of when it replays j, about s beats earlier on stage s (PP7: about 7 beats).
Equivalently, pages freed in the last s + 2 epochs cannot be reused by an early load on stage s.
4. Where it bites: short forwards happen when device KV is full. Device KV use in short forwards: quartiles 0.79 / 0.89 / 0.97
(long forwards 0.62 / 0.77 / 0.89). Early loads take pages exactly where admission is already short of them.
host CPU work (build + admit, launch, post-process)
host waits: upstream message or send credit
host waits for its own GPU (launch queue full)
GPU idle because the host is late
GPU idle: waits for upstream input
prefix KV load-back, host → GPU (H2D kernel)
load-back of that micro-batch issued on the host
next stage's forward waits on the flag (GPU-side)
early KV send to decode (RDMA, after the forward)
KV pages held earlier than today
